the learned counsel appearing for the parties.

2. In this writ petition, the petitioner is assailing the Notification dated 07.03.2023 (Annexure-F)
passed by respondent No.1-State and Endorsement dated 05.02.2024 (Annexure-P), issued by the respondent-Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Board (for short, KIADB).
NC: 2024:KHC:50672 3.

Sri. Vishwanath R.Hegde, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner contended that, the Impugned Endorsement dated 05.02.2024 (Annexure-P) issued by respondent No.2, rejecting the objections raised by the petitioner, opposing the acquisition proceedings, while issuing Final Notification dated 07.03.2023, under Section 28(4) of Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act,
1966 (for short, KIAD Act) is not proceeded by an enquiry and therefore, sought for joint measurement to be made insofar as the land in question and take decision in the matter in accordance with law.
4. The said submission was opposed by Sri.Dildar Shiralli, learned counsel appearing for respondent Nos.2 and 3 that, the Award Notice has already issued under Section 29(2) of KIAD Act.

5. In the light of the submission made by the learned counsel appearing for the parties, on careful examination of the Endorsement dated 05.02.2024 (Annexure-P), would indicate that no joint survey has been conducted at the instance of the petitioner to determine the compensation that may B. M. Ambarisha vs The State Of Karnataka on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8061847/
2 be paid or NC: 2024:KHC:50672 in respect of the validity of acquisition proceedings are concerned.

sentences.text: 6. In that view of the matter, taking into consideration the declaration of law made by this Court in WP.No.26546/2023 disposed of on 26.09.2024, I am of the view that, the respondent-KIADB be permitted to consider the objections filed by the petitioner at Annexure-D dated 26.04.2022 and take decision in the matter by passing the Final notification there under.

In the result, I pass the following:
ORDER i. Writ petition is allowed.

ii. Final Notification dated 07.03.2023 (Annexure-F) passed by respondent-authorities, under Section 28(4) of the KIAD Act, is hereby set-aside and the matter stands remanded to respondent No.2 to take decision in the matter, after considering the Objection dated 26.04.2022 (Annexure-D), filed by the petitioner and to take decision accordingly.
NC: 2024:KHC:50672 iii.
The said exercise shall be completed within three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.

SD/-
(E.S.INDIRESH) JUDGE PK CT: BHK B. M. Ambarisha vs The State Of Karnataka on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8061847/
